## MGIT EEE Students Visit IIT Hyderabad for Industry Lecture on Smart Grids

News Date : 08 Aug 2025News ReportStudents ofB.Tech VII-Semester Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE)fromMahatma Gandhi Institute of Technology (Autonomous), Hyderabad, along with their faculty members, visited theIndian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH)for an industry lecture and academic interaction.The visit aimed to provide students with deeper insights intoemerging trends, research opportunities, and practical applications in the power and energy sector.The highlight of the program was an engaging lecture byDr. Ramakrishna Kappagantuon“Powering the Future: Exploring Smart Grid Research and Career Opportunities”. His talk covered:Fundamentals of the electric grid and its evolutionThe significance and need for smart gridsEmerging research domains and future trendsDiverse career opportunities in power systems, energy management, and policy analysisStudents actively interacted with researchers at IITH, exploring opportunities forcollaborative projects in smart grid technologies. The session sparked enthusiasm among participants, inspiring them to align their academic learning withreal-world applications.The visit was bothinformative and motivating, reinforcing the importance ofinnovation, research, and skill developmentin shaping the future of the energy sector.

Students ofB.Tech VII-Semester Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE)fromMahatma Gandhi Institute of Technology (Autonomous), Hyderabad, along with their faculty members, visited theIndian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH)for an industry lecture and academic interaction.
The visit aimed to provide students with deeper insights intoemerging trends, research opportunities, and practical applications in the power and energy sector.
The highlight of the program was an engaging lecture byDr. Ramakrishna Kappagantuon“Powering the Future: Exploring Smart Grid Research and Career Opportunities”. His talk covered:
- Fundamentals of the electric grid and its evolution
- The significance and need for smart grids
- Emerging research domains and future trends
- Diverse career opportunities in power systems, energy management, and policy analysis
Students actively interacted with researchers at IITH, exploring opportunities forcollaborative projects in smart grid technologies. The session sparked enthusiasm among participants, inspiring them to align their academic learning withreal-world applications.
The visit was bothinformative and motivating, reinforcing the importance ofinnovation, research, and skill developmentin shaping the future of the energy sector.
